notes.title: Server List Display Broken After UE 5.5 Update (SOLVED)
notes.notes:
[p][b]Breaking News![/b]
Just a few hours ago, I discovered a very unpleasant issue — the server list display is currently not working. This came as a complete surprise to me, as I haven’t touched any code related to that functionality. After updating to Unreal Engine version 5.5, the online subsystem stopped functioning correctly and no longer displays created sessions properly.[/p][p]Once again, I want to say a HUGE THANK YOU to Epic Games for breaking something critically important in the engine with every new update.[/p][p]I’ve made a decision for myself — this will be the last engine version upgrade for this project. From now on, it will remain on version 5.5 for as long as technically possible. Version updates have started causing far too many problems.[/p][p]Right now, I’m working on fixing the issue with the server list display. In PvE mode, when you host your own server, everything works as expected.[/p][p]Stay tuned for updates.[/p]

notes.title: Rapid Impact Upgraded to UE5.5 – Performance, Weather, and Visuals Revamped
notes.notes:
[p][b]Hello everyone![/b][/p][p]I’m excited to introduce one of the biggest updates for [i]Rapid Impact[/i], focusing on atmosphere, visuals, and performance:[/p][list][*][p][b]Upgraded to Unreal Engine 5.5[/b][/p][/*][*][p][b]New and more efficient real-time day/night and weather system.[/b] Time of day and weather are now randomized for each match.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Flashlight added[/b] (default key: [b]L[/b])[/p][/*][*][p][b]Ultra-wide scalability settings[/b] – the game now offers a massive range of performance and quality options. Low-end GPUs can enjoy solid image quality and high FPS on the [i]Low[/i] preset, while high-end cards will be pushed to their limits on [i]Ultra[/i], delivering stunning visuals for graphics enthusiasts.[/p][p]This scalability system took a lot of time to build. Epic Games has been slowly removing or breaking support for low-end optimization features in recent engine updates in favor of their “super mega ultra” tech. But as long as I can, I will continue to support a wide range of hardware so more players can enjoy the game – even if it gets harder with each Unreal version.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Map changes[/b] – denser vegetation and more trees in the central zone make the environment feel more abandoned and atmospheric. Trees also now act as natural cover, preventing long-range line-of-sight across the entire map.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Vulkan support added[/b] for SteamOS and Steam Deck. Windows users can also try Vulkan by adding launch options in the game’s properties. I’ll later add a proper in-game toggle for switching rendering modes.[/p][/*][/list][hr][/hr][p][b]Helpful Tips for Low-End GPUs (4GB VRAM or similar):[/b][/p][list][*][p]If you enable [b]FSR[/b], it’s [b]highly recommended to fully restart the game[/b] afterwards. For unknown reasons, some GPUs experience a significant FPS drop right after enabling FSR, but a restart fixes it and restores expected performance gains.[/p][/*][*][p]If you get a [b]FATAL ERROR[/b] on first launch after the update, delete the RapidImpact folder located at C:\\Users\\YourName\\AppData\\Local.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Don’t chase the ULTRA preset[/b] unless you have a high-end GPU. It’s meant for future-proofing and is only recommended for cards like the [b]RTX 2080 SUPER or better[/b]. If there’s demand, I can add full [b]ray tracing[/b] support to the Ultra preset (expect an additional 15% performance hit, but with uncompromised lighting and reflections).[/p][/*][*][p]For cards like the [b]GTX 1650[/b], I recommend lowering your resolution to [b]1600x900[/b], even with FSR enabled, to maintain a stable 60 FPS. Depending on your full system specs, you may still get playable 1080p on Low with or without FSR. According to Epic, UE5 games aren’t even supposed to run on these cards – but I’ve put a lot of effort into making it possible to enjoy the game with decent visuals on low-end hardware. Unlike Fortnite’s Low preset (where shadows are completely disabled), [i]Rapid Impact[/i] tries to retain visual quality even on Low.[/p][/*][/list][hr][/hr][p][b]P.S.[/b]
Yes, I remember my promise to add [b]weapon attachments, upgrades[/b], and [b]character progression[/b]. I was waiting for a major update to the core framework my project is based on – and that update is finally here. Now I can start implementing these systems. Big gameplay and content-focused updates are coming next. I believe the core of the project is now solid in terms of visuals and performance, and it's time to shift focus to gameplay features and new content.[/p][p]Stay tuned for more updates!

notes.title: Atmospheric Upgrade: Dynamic Lighting & Weather System
notes.notes:
Hi everyone.

In this update, I decided to add dynamic changes in time of day and weather. Yes, FPS performance has dropped, but the world has become even more diverse, and the atmosphere has reached a new level. On my end, I’ve already done a lot to optimize performance for such fully dynamic lighting. In terms of visual quality vs. performance, the project is already ahead of many counterparts.

Additionally, I’ve expanded the range of graphics settings so that the game can be adjusted to suit as many hardware configurations as possible.

For now, players spawn in the world at a random time of day. Soon, I’ll add an option to choose which part of the day you'd like to spawn in, and I’ll also add a flashlight to make nighttime gameplay more convenient.

At the same time, I’m working on the mechanics for gaining experience and in-game currency. In upcoming updates, you’ll be able to earn XP and currency, which can be spent on weapons and upgrades.

Attaching a video showcasing the game’s new dynamic atmosphere.

notes.title: Important Notice: Review Keys Blocked Due to Misuse
notes.notes:
Friends, I've received information about [b]attempts to sell game keys that were distributed to reviewers.[/b] All such keys have now been blocked, and from this point on, the distribution of review keys will be strictly limited for two reasons:

- [b]Attempts to sell them.[/b]
- A low amount of content and reviews compared to the number of keys distributed.
Anyone who wants to make a review or test the game can use the free playtest version or steam curator channel. In the future, I may create a separate demo version of the game for this purpose, if necessary.

[u]Addition from April 26:[/u]
- [b]Only the keys[/b] that were specifically distributed[b] for reviewers for free[/b] to review the game have been [b]revoked[/b].
- [b]This does not affect anyone who purchased the game through the Steam store.[/b]
- If you bought the game from a [b]third-party marketplace[/b] and received a notification that your key [b]was revoked[/b], it means [b]scammers sold you[/b] a copy of the game that was intended for [b]review purposes only, not for sale.[/b]
   [b] [u]Advice:[/u] Never buy Steam games from third-party marketplaces.[/b]

notes.title: Update from April 24, 2025
notes.notes:
- A small update to the AI bots that fixes some behavior bugs.

P.S. Why am I spending so much time working on bots instead of adding new features to the game? Since the player count is still relatively low, I want the bots to act as filler in the game world, and I want their behavior to closely mimic that of real players. Over time, as the number of online players grows, I’ll reduce the number of bots in the game - or remove them entirely, leaving them as an optional feature.

P.P.S. I’m now starting work on the experience and in-game currency system, which will allow players to upgrade different weapon branches and unlock new guns and upgrades. This will include a weapon progression tree and an in-game shop. As a reference, I’ll be using the system from World of Tanks for now.

notes.title: Post-Release Thoughts and Reflections
notes.notes:
Hello friends.
The first weekend after release has passed, and I want to share some thoughts with you.

First of all, thank you for showing interest in my project. I can see it in the [b]massive increase in wishlists[/b] - tens of times more than before. I’ve also noticed a [b]huge spike in traffic[/b] to the game’s page.
Secondly, I read all your feedback, and I always try to respond first to those who left negative reviews - because [b]I take it personally[/b]. Yes, maybe some people were hoping to see a multiplayer version of STALKER 2, 90% complete, packed with weapons and maps, bug-free and perfectly polished. Or maybe someone expected this to be my answer to Escape from Tarkov... But in the [b]release post[/b], I believe I honestly and objectively described the [b]current state of the game[/b] and what it really is.

[b]You might ask - why release it in this state, and what’s the point?[/b]

The main idea was to give you the opportunity to be part of the development from the earliest stage. To [b]create this project[/b] from the beginning [b]based on your feedback and suggestions[/b]. That’s why your impressions and reviews are so important to me.
I could’ve worked on this project for several more years without showing it to anyone, doing everything the way I personally think is right. That’s how many studios and producers do it. And in the end, they create a game for one person - the producer or game designer who made it. Players don’t need it, because it wasn’t made for them. I don’t want to go down that path.

[b]You might also ask - why didn’t I make it free?[/b]

First, I intentionally decided [b]against a free-to-play model[/b], because I don’t like that kind of monetization. I don’t want to sell characters or weapon skins or character cosmetics for money. I especially don’t want to see loot boxes or gacha systems in the game.
There’s nothing truly free in this world. Playing any “free” game usually ends up costing much more than a game you buy once. At least for now, I don’t see a future for this project as a free-to-play game.
Second, [b]I want to build a kind of closed community around this project.[/b] Even if there are fewer people in this “club,” they will be better. I don’t want to be distracted by the noise of the crowd—random people leaving thousands of contradictory reviews and suggestions… or just trolling.
Buying the project now is your entry fee into this “club.” [b]You can get your money back[/b] if, after buying and playing the game, you don’t see its potential or future. You have two hours of playtime or two weeks to decide. [b]So don’t be afraid to give it a try[/b].
I understand it’s hard to buy something almost blindly. There aren’t many reviews yet. Not many streams or videos either. But fortunately, you’re fully protected on this Steam platform. I’ve also sent out [b]dozens of keys to influencers so they can create reviews for you[/b].
Lastly, as I’ve mentioned before, [b]I didn’t run a Kickstarter or anything like that[/b] for this project. I prefer the approach where you immediately get something tangible, and you see the development process and participate in it right away. [b]Think of buying the game as a similar kind of support[/b] - just like on Kickstarter or any other funding platform - except you don’t have to wait, and [b]you get at least something right now.[/b]
I have no investors or publisher. I’m spending my own money on the project, and [b]most of the money[/b] from game sales, at least in the beginning, [b]will go toward the game’s development[/b]. I already have a long wishlist of add-ons I want to purchase and implement into the game as soon as possible.
In the meantime, I’m working on patches and improvements based on your feedback to refine what’s already in the game - so we can move forward calmly and confidently.
Stay tuned for updates, friends.
See you in the world of Rapid Impact.

notes.title: Rapid Impact is almost here
notes.notes:
Greetings, friends.
This post marks the release of this project in Early Access. At last, I can present it to you and let you try it out.

Yes, right now it's a relatively small project, with the core gameplay already implemented. But even now, you can play it with your friends — cooperatively, against AI bots, or against each other. Several core modes are already available, along with a few weapons to choose from and one large, detailed map. It may not be much, but it's the foundation of the project.

I want to build this project together with you — based on your feedback and suggestions. I’ll be watching the discussions here on the forum, and I’ll be in touch with you directly. Each of you has a chance to influence the future development of the project. If someone’s idea receives strong community support, I’ll do my best to implement it in the best possible way.
There are no layers of managers and producers between you and me — no one to bury your feedback or steer the project down the wrong path out of misguided instinct. When you speak here, you can be sure that your words will reach the creator directly — they will be heard and considered. I personally read every comment and every review.

Yes, I used templates and asset packs in the project. That helped me significantly speed up development and avoid many design pitfalls while building the core. But that doesn’t mean development was easy. Every template still needs to be adapted for the specific mechanics and feel of the game. That takes skill in working with someone else’s code and turning it into something of your own.
Even large companies reuse years-old frameworks and tools across projects. That’s standard in the game industry.

I hope this is just the beginning of a long journey we’ll take together. I truly believe we can create a great game — one that’s fun for you, your friends, and for me to play too.

I didn’t launch a Kickstarter campaign for this game. The only financial support I have comes through the Early Access sales. When you buy the game, you’re directly supporting me as the developer. I don’t have a publisher or investors — only my own money and my own heart invested into this project.

Thank you for being here. And see you soon.
The journey begins… today at EEST (UTC+3): 20:00
